advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile assert_cloud_scope_ready's extra checks (email-shape JIRA_USER, empty query_project) with the legacy assert_env_ready so the scope and ambient paths fail-close identically, or explicitly document the delta.
evidence: runtime.py assert_cloud_scope_ready: `_assert_cloud_user_is_email(scope.user)` and `if not scope.query_project.strip(): raise BackendEnvError(...)`

backend.py:231-238 legacy Cloud assert_env_ready only checks `("JIRA_URL", settings.url), ("JIRA_USER", settings.user), ("JIRA_API_TOKEN", settings.api_token)` with no email-shape or query_project check
The ticket names an approved delta (empty Cloud read scope fails closed), but the email-format check is an additional, undocumented behavior added only on the scope path
advisory.finding: assert_cloud_scope_ready (scope path) enforces two checks the legacy ambient assert_env_ready does not: JIRA_USER must be an email and query_project must be non-empty. The same JiraBackend therefore fails-closed differently depending on whether it was built with a captured scope or in the legacy ambient path, a silent behavior divergence between the two code paths of one method.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make DC build_backend fail-closed symmetry explicit — either call assert_datacenter_scope_ready in _build_datacenter or document that DC defers readiness to assert_env_ready/first-call.
evidence: _build_cloud: `assert_cloud_scope_ready(s)` before constructing transport/backend
_build_datacenter: no readiness assertion; `if transport is not None: return JiraDataCenterBackend(...)` and otherwise builds a `_LazyDataCenterClient` and returns without asserting scope
build_backend docstring: "build_backend (Cloud) and the built backend's assert_env_ready raise ... BEFORE any transport/network call" — the fail-closed-at-build guarantee is scoped to Cloud only
advisory.finding: build_backend fails-closed asymmetrically by provider: _build_cloud calls assert_cloud_scope_ready(s) unconditionally before returning, but _build_datacenter performs no assert_datacenter_scope_ready at build time (relying on the lazy client / explicit assert_env_ready). A DC runtime with missing base_url/JIRA_PAT returns a fully-constructed backend from build_backend, while the equivalent Cloud runtime raises.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either thread scope.comment_max_chars / scope.jira_cli_timeout into the built backend/sanitizer/acli, or drop the unused captured fields and correct the docstring to scope the 'resolved ONCE' claim to project/query/auth.
evidence: runtime.py ReconcilerSettings fields `comment_max_chars: int` and `jira_cli_timeout: int` are captured in _runtime_from_snapshot

backend.py (jira_datacenter):250-255 still `self._comment_max_chars = resolve_comment_max_chars()` (ambient load_config) when unset — the captured scope.comment_max_chars is never passed to _DCSanitizer
acli_subprocess.py:86 `value = load_config().reconciler.jira_cli_timeout` — timeout still resolved ambiently, not from scope.jira_cli_timeout
advisory.finding: ReconcilerSettings captures comment_max_chars and jira_cli_timeout, but neither is threaded into the built backend: the DC sanitizer still lazily calls resolve_comment_max_chars() (an ambient load_config re-read) and the Cloud acli path still resolves the timeout ambiently. The captured limit/timeout values are dead, contradicting the module docstring's 'resolved ONCE here, not re-read from ambient env/config' and the ticket's 'timeout/limits ... remain stable'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm no incidental attribute probe on _LazyDataCenterClient forces premature real-client construction (guard dunders / narrow __getattr__ to known client methods), or document the exact deferral boundary.
evidence: `def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Any: return getattr(self._resolve(), name)`
_resolve builds the real client and can raise BackendEnvError on empty PAT

The comment in build_client_from_settings notes Protocol isinstance on <=3.11 evaluates properties via hasattr — a similar incidental attribute probe on this lazy client would force real-client construction earlier than 'first real network call'
advisory.finding: _LazyDataCenterClient.__getattr__ proxies EVERY otherwise-missing attribute (including dunders and probe attributes) to the lazily-built real jira.JIRA client, which triggers construction (and the fail-closed missing-PAT raise inside build_client_from_settings) on the first access of any unknown attribute — potentially an incidental hasattr/isinstance probe rather than a genuine network call.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a DC runtime with missing base_url or absent JIRA_PAT fails closed with the typed BackendEnvError before client construction.
evidence: search for `assert_datacenter_scope_ready` in tests returned (no matches)
runtime.py:369-390 `assert_datacenter_scope_ready(...)` raises BackendEnvError when `url`/`JIRA_PAT` missing — a new fail-closed contract
DC tests (lines 75-84, 44-55) only assert the happy path `backend.project == 'DIG'`
search for `_assert_cloud_user_is_email` in tests returned (no matches)
runtime.py:357-366 raises BackendEnvError when JIRA_USER lacks `@`/local/domain
the autouse fixture pins JIRA_USER to a valid email (line 59), so no test hits the invalid branch
advisory.finding: The Data Center fail-closed readiness path (assert_datacenter_scope_ready: missing base_url and/or missing JIRA_PAT) is never exercised. Cloud has test_empty_cloud_scope_fails_closed and test_missing_auth_fails_closed, but there is no DC analogue asserting that a DC compose+assert_env_ready with an empty base_url or absent JIRA_PAT raises the typed BackendEnvError before any client build.
merged_from: The non-email JIRA_USER rejection (_assert_cloud_user_is_email) is untested. This is a distinct new fail-closed branch in assert_cloud_scope_ready — a JIRA_USER that is present but not an email must raise BackendEnvError — yet no test supplies a non-email JIRA_USER.
scenarios: A DC operator omits reconciler.base_url or JIRA_PAT; regression could let build proceed to a real client build / network call.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add test_datacenter_missing_url_or_pat_fails_closed mirroring the Cloud fail-closed tests, monkeypatching JIRA_PAT/base_url and asserting a BackendEnvError from assert_env_ready().

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten fail-closed assertions to `pytest.raises(BackendEnvError)` (or the specific typed family) rather than `exc.type is not AssertionError`.
evidence: test_empty_cloud_scope_fails_closed_before_transport line 159 `assert exc.type is not AssertionError`
test_missing_auth_fails_closed line 166 `assert exc.type is not AssertionError`
runtime docstring/AC4: raises a TYPED BackendEnvError 'never a bare AssertionError / KeyError'
advisory.finding: Fail-closed tests assert only `exc.type is not AssertionError`, which is too weak to pin the contract. The AC requires a TYPED BackendEnvError (subclassing RuntimeError), but these tests accept ANY non-AssertionError exception — a regression raising a bare KeyError, TypeError, or unrelated ValueError from a different point (even before the guard) would still pass.
scenarios: A regression that fails closed with the wrong (untyped/generic) error, or fails at an unintended earlier point, still satisfies the assertion.
advisory.suggested_fix: Import BackendEnvError and use `with pytest.raises(BackendEnvError):` for the empty-scope and missing-auth tests.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Narrow the immutability assertion to the concrete FrozenInstanceError/AttributeError raised by frozen-dataclass assignment.
evidence: line 82 `with pytest.raises((AttributeError, TypeError, Exception)):`
the intended contract is that assigning to a frozen dataclass field raises dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError (a subclass of AttributeError)
dropped.finding: test_compose_returns_immutable_settings uses pytest.raises((AttributeError, TypeError, Exception)); including bare Exception makes the assertion satisfied by essentially any raised error, so it does not specifically verify the frozen-dataclass FrozenInstanceError on assignment.
